At MiniMed, you can begin a lifelong career of exploration and innovation, while helping make a difference in the lives of people living with diabetes around the globe. You'll lead with purpose, breaking down barriers to innovation for a more connected, compassionate world.

About The Role

MiniMed is seeking an experienced Principal Biomedical Engineer to join our Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM) Sensor R&D team. This role will provide technical leadership in the development, and improvement of next-generation CGM sensor technologies.

In this role, you will lead complex technical investigations, develop and execute data-driven experimental strategies to characterize component- and system-level performance, and translate technical insights into actionable improvements that influence the design and reliability of next-generation Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM) sensors. The role emphasizes structured problem-solving methodologies, including DMAIC, and the application of Design for Reliability and Manufacturability (DRM) principles to drive product robustness, performance, and continuous improvement.

The ideal candidate will bring a strong background in medical device product development, preferably with expertise in electrochemical sensors and related medical device technologies. The candidate should demonstrate exceptional technical problem-solving and analytical capabilities, proven cross-functional leadership, and experience driving product improvements through systematic root cause investigations and Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) processes.

Responsibilities may include the following and other duties may be assigned.

Lead complex technical investigations across all phases of product development, including post-market performance, to identify root causes, characterize failure mechanisms, and drive product improvements.
Develop and implement advanced tools, methodologies, and structured problem-solving approaches (DMAIC) to address complex component- and system-level technical challenges.
Troubleshoot and characterize performance anomalies in microfabricated electrochemical biosensors through systematic experimentation, advanced analytical techniques, and data-driven analysis.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including Design, Manufacturing, Quality, and Regulatory, to develop and implement effective technical solutions that enhance product performance and reliability.
Design, develop, and optimize test methods, measurement techniques, and fixtures to improve product characterization, diagnostic capabilities, and testing efficiency.
Develop and execute verification, validation, and reliability test strategies to assess product performance, design robustness, and long-term reliability.
Conduct hands-on laboratory investigations, interpret experimental findings, and translate technical insights into actionable design recommendations and corrective actions.
Prepare and maintain technical documentation, including experimental protocols, investigation reports, test methods, and engineering assessments.
Evaluate product designs against performance specifications, regulatory requirements, and applicable national and international standards.
Support sustaining engineering and continuous improvement initiatives through technical impact assessments, risk evaluations, design reviews, and Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) processes.
Designs, develops and provides safety testing, repair, and maintenance of biomedical equipment.
Ensures that the biomedical equipment is in compliance with applicable regulatory requirements and quality control standards.
Design studies and conduct research on enzyme reactions and the effects of organic compounds on biological processes.
Participate in activities such as compound screening and compound optimization programs, and developing and running enzyme assays.

Minimum Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in biomedical engineering, chemical engineering or related engineering field with at least 7 years of experience, or an advanced degree with at least 5 years of experience.

Nice To Have

Medical Device product development: Demonstrated experience developing electrochemical medical devices within design controls and Quality Management systems; familiarity with FSA requirements, ISO 13485, risk analysis and FMEA.
Failure Analysis & Problem Solving: Demonstrated experience in leading complex, cross-functional failure analysis investigations using structured problem-solving methodologies such as DMAIC, root cause analysis, fault-tree analysis, and hypothesis-driven experimentation.
Technical leadership: Proven ability to lead complex projects with limited oversight, manage multiple priorities, influence cross-functional stakeholders, and coach or mentor engineers in structured problem-solving and failure analysis.
Experience in electrochemical sensor design and development in an R&D environment
Experience leading complex root-cause investigations within medical device industry
Direct experience in characterization, design of experiments and data analysis methodologies (T-test, ANOVA and significance testing at a minimum)
Working knowledge of in-vitro and in-vivo testing of subcutaneous medical devices
Certification in DMAIC or equivalent Scientific Method problem solving for root cause analysis
Experience with statistical analysis of data (Ex. Minitab, JMP, Matlab, etc.)
Capable of working on multiple projects in a deadline driven environment
Greenbelt in DRM, Six Sigma
Cleanroom procedural experience

MiniMed offers a competitive salary and flexible benefits package

At MiniMed, we put people first. A commitment to our employees lives at the core of our values: We recognize their contributions. They share in the success they help create. new_jobs.title: Entry Civil Engineer
new_jobs.description:
The intent of this job posting is to fill one (1) regular, full-time position and establish an eligibility list which may be used to fill current and future, permanent and limited-term, vacancies for up to two (2) years.

We are posting this opportunity for an Entry Civil Engineer along with a Journey Civil Engineer position. The department will be filling only one position at either level. If you are interested in also being considered for a Journey Civil Engineer, you will need to apply to that requisition separately.

Application Preparation: As part of the application process, candidates will be required to answer four (4) supplemental questions when submitting their application. Please be advised, "Refer to resume" responses will not be accepted.

Purpose

Under general supervision, assists in performing minor to moderately complex civil/structural engineering core responsibilities, including problem resolution/project assignments, in the most efficient, safe and cost-effective manner, and that comply with regulatory requirements and restrictions.

Nature and Scope

There are four (4) levels in this job classification series that have similar job content but with progressively more challenging degrees and levels of skill, responsibility, knowledge, experience and qualification requirements:

Flex Classifications (that permit progression from lower-level classes to higher level classes without examination based upon assessment of an individual's experience and performance) within the series:

Entry:
Incumbent acquires knowledge, skills and abilities to perform the tasks associated within the series but are not yet demonstrating these at the Journey level.
Journey:
Incumbent is demonstrating the required skills and knowledge to independently perform the full scope of the job.

Non-Flex Classifications (that promote from lower-level classes to higher level classes and require an examination, such as an interview, based upon individual experience and performance) within the series:

Senior:
Advanced journey level resource who is responsible for advanced assignments, as dictated by the work needing to be performed; may serve in a lead capacity.
Principal:
Subject matter expert/lead level and is responsible for leading the most advanced work, as dictated by the work needing to be performed.

Entry to Journey: Incumbents at the entry level are required to successfully “progress” to the journey level within 60 months of appointment to remain within the job series.
Seniors and Principals must be hired through a promotional process and do not automatically progress from lower levels in the series.

Duties and Responsibilities

Assists and learns, under the guidance of senior staff, to develop civil construction drawings and mapping related to high voltage electrical transmission and distribution systems for both underground and overhead systems.
Assists in the Civil design work for various SMUD assets, which may include completing studies and calculations of minor projects varying from drainage to structural design; applies national, state, and local agency standards and guidelines while completing engineering work.
Assists in contract and project development under the supervision of other engineering staff.
Supports field crews and contractors to ensure construction is in accordance with SMUD requirements and plans.
Assists and learns to complete project tasks according to industry standards and with industry specific tools including PLS CADD.
Assists and learns to complete design tasks that meet ASCE, ACI, NESC, CPUC General Orders, and company standards.
Assists in the review of developments and encroachments within the Transmission Line rights-of-way.
Learns how to use the full suite of Microsoft products and other applications such as Bluebeam or Adobe to edit PDFs.
Assists with basic design assignments, draft plans, revise drawings, and update maps using AutoCAD and Civil 3D.
Performs other related duties as needed to include working outside of typical business hours when necessary.

Required Education

Bachelor's degree in civil engineering from an accredited college or university.

Required Experience Qualifications

At least one (1+) year of progressively responsible relevant work experience in the design, construction, or maintenance of civil or structural assets.

Knowledge Of

Basic theories, principles and practices of civil/structural engineering design; basic theories, principles and regulations governing safety and construction of civil/structural systems and facilities; basic fundamentals, procedures and practices related to construction/fabrication/installation methods, equipment and materials; basic computer aided drafting and design software (such as AutoCAD); basic fundamentals, procedures and practices related to engineering mathematics and statistical analysis techniques; safety policies, practices and procedures; pertinent federal, state, and local codes, laws, and regulations; office procedures, methods, and equipment including computers and applicable software applications such as word processing, spreadsheets, and databases; English grammar, punctuation and vocabulary standards.

Skills To

Learn to use state of the art computer software to design civil/structural systems and facilities; maintain computer databases for collection, interpretation and reporting of data; learn to read and interpret engineering documents and drawings, plans, diagrams, and specifications; learn to assess situations, documents and data for conformance to established policy and procedures; gather data from appropriate sources and identify relevant factors; learn to interpret, assess and apply pertinent policies, procedures, regulations, and requirements; learn to interpret, clarify, understand and evaluate verbal/written information and ideas; learn fundamentals, procedures and practices related to engineering economics; learn fundamentals and practices of economic assessment of projects and programs; learn techniques and practices for cost benefit analyses; learn procedures and practices for overseeing contractor’s work activities; learn techniques and practices for problem research and resolution; ensure adherence to established safety policies, practices and procedures; learn to schedule and prioritize own work assignments to meet expected timeframes; learn to compile and prepare technical, statistical and/or analytical reports and presentations; communicate effectively orally and in writing internally/externally; establish and maintain effective working relationships internally/externally.

Desirable Qualifications

Knowledge of and experience with electric utility transmission and distribution systems and/or public works infrastructure design and construction.
Experience in the design and construction of reinforced concrete foundations and steel structures.
Experience developing engineering and/or construction design standards, as well as preparing engineering and/or construction specifications and procedures.
Proficiency in Autodesk AutoCAD, Microsoft Excel, structural analysis software, and other engineering software tools used in civil engineering practice.
Experience in contract administration and construction administration.
Engineer In Training (EIT) certification
Professional registration in civil and/or structural engineering in the state of California.

Physical Requirements

Applicants must be able to perform the essential job functions with or without a reasonable accommodation.

As the nation's sixth-largest community-owned electric service provider, we're proud of our reputation as one of the best places to work in Sacramento. Our employees tell us in our engagement surveys they're "Happy, satisfied and engaged" which helps create a workplace that best serves our customers. new_jobs.title: Senior Civil Engineer
new_jobs.description:
WHY JOIN #TEAMRC

WHY WORK FOR RC ENGINEERING?

The Engineering Services Department consists of three separate sections Project Management/Project Delivery, Land Development, and Transportation, with a total of twenty-four (24) staff members that span various roles.

From its earliest days, the City of Rancho Cucamonga was dubbed the "City with a Plan" and over the past forty years, we have been creating a World Class Community. So, what does this have to do with engineering? Everything! Engineering is more than simply building and maintaining roads, it's about providing the built environment that is the context for the people and the places of our lives. As we move into our fifth decade as a City, we are continuing to build a World Class Community for our children and grandchildren to enjoy. One that takes the best parts of our past and continues growing and reimagining itself for the future. We are excited to have the opportunity to play a big part in what is coming next for our community. Whether it is through high quality design and construction of the built environment, by ensuring that our environment stays clean and sustainable, or by providing reliable utility services to residents and businesses.

What You Will Be Doing Here At Team Rc

THE POSITION

Are you ready to take your engineering career to the next level? We are currently seeking a dynamic individual to join our team to fill a key management and high-level technical role. There is currently one vacancy, and depending on qualifications, the top candidate will be chosen to fill a Senior role.

The Project Management/Project Delivery Team consists of three assistant engineers, two associate engineers and one principal engineer. Reporting directly to the Principal Engineer, the Senior Engineer position offers the chance to make a significant impact and operate with a high degree of autonomy.

The Senior Civil Engineer is responsible for bringing a high level of technical expertise to assist our Associate and Assistant Engineers through complex capital projects. The ideal candidate for this role will embody a facilitation mindset and will also be well versed in a broad range of engineering skill sets related to Project Delivery, including but not limited to complex project and contract management, sound cost estimating strategies, creating economics of scale, understanding constructability, and strategic planning.

Capital Management

The Capital Management Section is responsible for the preparation and implementation of the City’s Major Projects Program (MPP). This includes the design, construction, and installation of various public improvements throughout the City. Typical projects include street improvements, storm drain construction, railroad crossing improvements, and facility construction or upgrades. The Capital Management section also manages funding programs related to the implementation of the MPP and other operational functions including Measure I 2010-2040, State Gas Tax and Road Maintenance and Repair Funding, along with State and Federal grants.

YOUR IMPACT

Notable Projects You May Work On

As Part Of The Engineering Services Team, You’ll Have The Opportunity To Be a Part Of Rewarding Projects That Make a Visible Impact In Our Community. Some Of The Exciting Projects Currently Underway At The City Of Rancho Cucamonga Include

Pavement Management Program Implementation - A city-wide assessment of pavement condition to be able to best plan for future CIP projects and improve our average Pavement Condition Index (PCI).
Active Transportation Plan and Local Roadway Safety Plan Implementation - Two separate planning efforts to set the foundation for prioritizing future infrastructure projects for both the City’s CIP and future grant applications.
City Center Boulevards Project - Oversee design and construction for this transformative project on Haven Avenue and Foothill Boulevard. This project aims to create a City Center adjacent to the City's Civic Center and planned developments along two of the City's primary corridors. The project will remove on vehicular lane to construct a frontage road with complete street elements including enhanced landscaping, street furniture, on-street parking, bicycle facilities, and transit stops.
Phase 2 Heritage Park Bridge Replacement - The reconstruction of two bridges currently servicing pedestrians, equestrians.
Etiwanda Grade Separation Project - A $125 Million investment to construct a new grade separated overcrossing along Etiwanda Avenue over the railroad tracks. Tasks will include identifying funding, closing out the right of way process, and overseeing construction.
Etiwanda Creek Bridges Project - Lead design, environmental clearance and permitting, and construction for one new culvert on Whittram Avenue and a widened culvert on Arrow Avenue.
General Plan Implementation - Reimagining of street cross-sections along our two largest corridors, and ensuring our vision is communicated to developers to achieve desired quality of life improvements for our community.

You enjoy sharing your knowledge with and fostering growth in members of your team.

Description

SCHEDULE

Night Shift

4x10 Schedule

LOCATION

There will be a 4 week onsite training in Rancho Bernardo, CA and then the job will be hybrid.

Why Millennium Health?

Millennium Health LLC is an accredited specialty laboratory with more than a decade of experience in medication monitoring and drug testing services, helping clinicians monitor the use and misuse of prescription medications and illicit drugs. The testing is used by healthcare professionals to obtain objective information about patients’ recent use of prescription medications and/or illicit drugs and helps monitor the effectiveness of treatment plans. Everyone that joins our team is key to our ability to support the clinicians and patients.

General Summary

The Clinical Laboratory Scientist, Data Review will review chromatographic data and calculated results obtained from a variety of standardized urinalysis tests in a toxicology laboratory for the detection of prescription and illicit drugs using advanced LC-MS-MS technology and EIA; applies toxicological and chromatographic rule sets to determine acceptability of results; requests additional testing as necessary; approves reports and patient results to ordering physicians.

Essential Functions

The following are intended to be examples of the accountabilities for which the person in this position is responsible. This is not intended to be complete or all-inclusive and does not preclude management from assigning related functions for which the individual has demonstrated competency through performance.

Responsible for testing to troubleshoot result issues.
Reports laboratory test results for all test methods approved by CAP, NY and CLIA.
Ensures accuracy and quality of test results meeting required turnaround times.
Enters testing data and reviews chromatography and calculated results from a variety of standardized tests on urine samples using advanced LC-MS-MS technology and EIA for the detection of prescription and illicit drugs.
Evaluates the validity of results obtained, maintains proper records of results and creates a report of results.
Maintains quality control and LC-MS-MS chromatographic data prior to release or results to physicians.
Ensures that testing methods follow established quality control procedures.
Identifies, troubleshoots, documents and resolves test result issues.
Documents issues using the Laboratory Occurrence Management (LOM) form.
Acts as a resource to laboratory technicians, laboratory assistants and associate scientists.
Follows safe laboratory practices and participates in operational support activities necessary to maintain and optimize testing capabilities.
May oversee the duties of clinical laboratory technicians, clinical laboratory assistants and associate scientists who prepare specimens or perform other less complex procedures.
Participates in internal laboratory audits.

Secondary Accountabilities

Remains aware of evolving needs and opportunities, showing flexibility in doing whatever is appropriate to support the Company’s success. Pursues educational opportunities to maintain advanced and up-to-date knowledge in the field. Performs all other related duties as required and assigned and understands that the items in this description are not all-inclusive.

Requirements

SKILLS/KNOWLEDGE/ABILITIES

2+ years’ experience in high complexity testing; CLIA/CAP environment
Must maintain continuing education units required by California Department of Health Services
Knowledgeable in laboratory methods and techniques
Knowledgeable of equipment and supplies used in a laboratory
Proficient in MS applications (Word/Excel/PowerPoint/Outlook)
Strong interpersonal skills and ability to communicate with all levels of employees
Effective attention to detail with high degree of accuracy
Bachelor’s degree with current California CLS license
ASCP license highly preferred

Essential Physical & Mental Requirements

Sitting (85 %), walking (5 %), standing (10%), and lifting up to 20 lbs. Physical requirements will vary depending on departmental needs.
The employee is expected to read and understand standard operating procedures (SOPs)
The employee should be able to convert SOP instructions into work-related tasks.
The employee must be able to perform simple calculations as required in the SOP
The employee must be able to use judgment when there is a deviation in the system and effectively communicate any discrepancy to their supervisor.

Additional Physical & Mental Requirements

The employee is regularly exposed to high pressure/high stress situations, and therefore, must be able to thrive in this type of environment.
Must be able to tolerate a moderate noise level.
Must be able to work an extended schedule as needed.

Benefits

$100,000-108,000
10% Night Shift Differential for hours worked between 9pm and 4am.
$200 Weekend differential is added per weekend worked

About the role Construction Data Analysts turn Ironsite’s raw jobsite capture into answers contractors can act on. You’ll take the observations, activity labels, crew counts and productivity metrics coming off jobsites and turn them into dashboards, reports and insights. Superintendents, project executives and self-perform leads use these to run their work.

This role faces the customer. You’ll be on calls with contractor leadership, walking them through what the data says, why it matters and what to do about it. The best people in this seat are equal parts analyst and translator. They’re comfortable in the numbers, and just as comfortable explaining a productivity trend to someone with thirty years in the field and no patience for a bad metric.

What you’ll do Analysis and reporting

Turn structured data from Ironsite’s field capture pipeline (observations, activity labels, crew counts, productivity metrics) into clear deliverables that contractor teams can act on.
Own the reporting cycle for a portfolio of customer accounts: weekly summaries, milestone reports, and deep dives when something looks off.

Customer engagement

Join customer calls and present findings directly to superintendents, project executives and self-perform leads.
Defend the numbers and tell a coherent story about what’s happening on site.
Turn contractor questions into analysis tasks, and turn the results back into plain-language recommendations.

Dashboards

Build and maintain dashboards that contractor teams use regularly.

Data quality and field collaboration

Work closely with the field team to understand what was captured and how.
Flag data quality issues, and make sure the analysis reflects what actually happened on site.

Cross-project insights

Find patterns across projects, such as crew efficiency, trade coordination and production rates, and raise them before anyone asks.

What we’re looking for Required

Comfort with messy, real-world data. Construction sites aren’t clean environments, and neither is the data that comes off them.
Strong Excel or Google Sheets skills.
Construction experience, or the ability to pick up domain knowledge fast. You don’t need to know how to pour concrete, but you need to understand why cycle time matters.
Clear communication. You can write a concise summary, run a client call and explain a trend without jargon.
Attention to detail without losing the bigger picture. You notice when a number doesn’t look right, and you know when to flag it and when to keep moving.

Nice to have

Experience in construction technology, field operations or a related industry.
Familiarity with labor productivity benchmarks or earned value concepts.
A background in customer success or client-facing analytics.

What we offer A front-row seat to how construction is being re-measured and improved.
Direct access to field teams, customers and product. This isn’t a siloed analytics team.
Competitive compensation.
A small, focused team where your work shows up quickly in the product and in customer relationships.

new_jobs.title: Remote Medical AI Trainer
new_jobs.description:
Overview

We are currently hiring experienced clinicians to evaluate how frontier AI models handle real clinical work: an assessment and plan from a history and exam, a medication reconciliation with interaction checks, a triage decision, a discharge summary, patient education, or a clinical protocol. You bring the judgment you have built co signing a resident's note only after fixing the plan, catching the interaction the order set missed, and knowing when a presentation does not fit the obvious diagnosis. We bring the model output that judgment is needed to grade.

In this role, you will design challenging, realistic tasks drawn from your own practice, such as a SOAP note and plan for a constructed case, a medication reconciliation with interaction review, a triage decision with rationale, a discharge summary, a patient education handout, or a clinical protocol or standing order set, run them through frontier AI agents, and evaluate what comes back against a professional standard.

You will work with realistic professional files, the kind a practitioner in your field actually handles, which you assemble yourself. Some tasks are compact, built around a handful of files; others are larger scenarios that take several days to build. In every case the goal is the same: a task a competent professional in your field would complete correctly and a frontier model currently gets wrong.

This is not a traditional clinical role. You will be helping build better AI by putting your knowledge to work in a structured, flexible, fully remote environment. The work is long form and self directed, and clear written reasoning matters as much as technical depth.

Description

Design challenging, realistic clinical tasks drawn from your own day to day practice: the scenario, a prompt phrased the way you would brief a trusted colleague, and the supporting files a clinician would need (constructed or de identified histories, exam findings, labs, imaging reports, medication lists, prior notes), which you author yourself.
Run those tasks through frontier AI models and evaluate the deliverable they produce (the note, plan, reconciliation, summary or protocol) against the standard you would hold a colleague to.
Compare two model outputs on identical prompts and files, decide which performed better, and document where each fell short.
Write detailed grading rubrics that specify what a correct deliverable must contain, such as the right differential considered, the right red flags addressed, the right medication decisions, the right communication for the recipient, and explain in writing why a response passes or fails each one.
Flag concrete failures with evidence: unsupported assessments, missed contraindications or interactions, anchoring on the obvious diagnosis, fabricated or ignored data, unsafe or inappropriate communication, and off brief interpretation of the ask.
Contribute across your setting and adjacent ones, and review and refine tasks built by other clinicians.

Qualifications

2+ years of current or recent hands on clinical practice preferred. In progress Bachelors degree or higher.
Licensed clinician: RN, NP, PA, MD or DO, PharmD, or an allied health license with independent clinical judgment (for example respiratory therapy, physical therapy, midwifery). Licensed candidates may be asked to verify licensure during the assessment.
Depth in at least one setting or specialty: acute care and med surg, emergency, critical care, primary care and family medicine, pediatrics, obstetrics, behavioral health, geriatrics and long term care, perioperative, oncology, pharmacy.
Working understanding of adjacent settings, enough to know what those workflows involve and how they are run, so you can assess work outside your own unit and point out what was done correctly or incorrectly.
Reads and writes clinical documentation at a practitioner level and grounds decisions in current guidelines and the patient context rather than habit.

Additional Information

100% fully remote.
Can be part time or full time. Minimum requirement is 10 hours per week.

Doctors

new_jobs.description:
About Us

Scripps Research is a nonprofit biomedical institute ranked as one of the most influential in the world for its impact on innovation. We are celebrating our 100-year legacy in 2024. This significant milestone marks a century of seminal discoveries in immunology, infectious diseases (such as COVID-19, flu, HIV), neuroscience, heart disease, cancer, and more. Located in La Jolla, California, the institute houses six research departments, multiple Nobel laureates, a top-ranked graduate school and a leading postdoctoral training program. We work hand-in-hand with researchers of the Scripps Research Translational Institute and Calibr to merge foundational studies in biology, chemistry and computer science with translational science to produce pioneering drugs and advances in digital and precision medicine. Together, we cultivate new scientific leaders and expand the frontiers of knowledge to deliver medical breakthroughs impacting human health around the globe. If you have a passion for making a difference, this could be your opportunity to join our transformative team.

POSITION TITLE:
Research Assistant II

Position Summary

Plan and conduct complex research projects centered on 3D organoid culture, primary tissue cell isolation, and assay development in support of translational research programs. Independently perform non-routine procedures, develop new or improved techniques, design experimental approaches, analyze data, and interpret complex results. Operate sophisticated scientific lab equipment; plan and execute discrete projects or significant portions of larger research initiatives; may provide work direction and training to junior staff. Perform other related duties as required. This is an on site position based on our La Jolla, CA campus.

Responsibilities And Duties

Work under minimal supervision and independently execute a broad range of laboratory techniques, exercising judgment to adapt established methods to project-specific requirements. Receive direction on overall objectives, complex experimental features, and potential approaches.
Isolate primary cells from human tissue specimens, including biopsies and surgical resections. Establish, maintain, passage, and characterize 3D organoid cultures derived from primary human tissue, with particular attention to viability, growth kinetics, and phenotypic stability.
Develop, optimize, and validate cell-based assays in 3D organoid and primary cell systems, including readouts for viability, proliferation, differentiation, drug response, and disease-relevant phenotypes.
Maintain iPSC cultures including directed differentiation protocols and downstream characterization.
Process in vivo samples and integrate ex vivo data with in vitro experimental results.
Interpret and analyze experimental data; troubleshoot technical issues and modify procedures to improve robustness, throughput, or biological relevance.
Contribute to experimental design as part of broader research plans. May perform routine equipment maintenance and provide technical guidance and training to other team members.
Perform other related duties, tasks and responsibilities as required or assigned.

Position Requirements

Bachelor's degree in a relevant scientific discipline (cell biology, molecular biology, biomedical engineering, or related field), or an equivalent combination of education, training, and experience.
Requires 3-5 years of experience. Candidates possessing a master’s degree, 2+ years of experience required.
Hands-on experience with 3D organoid culture is required, including establishment from primary tissue, long-term maintenance, passaging, and characterization. Familiarity with patient-derived organoid systems strongly preferred.
Demonstrated experience isolating primary cells from human tissue (biopsy, surgical resection, or equivalent), including enzymatic/mechanical dissociation, viability assessment, and downstream culture establishment.
Proficiency with standard cell culture techniques.
Experience with imaging, flow cytometry, qPCR, or other relevant characterization methods.
Strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and ability to communicate experimental results clearly.

Physical Requirments

This position works in a laboratory or vivarium environment.
Details of established essential functions for this position will be addressed/discussed during the interview process.

Compensation

The expected hiring range for this position is $70,304 to $75,000 per year, commensurate with experience. Consideration will be given to experience that exceeds the listed requirements.

Comprehensive Benefits Include

Employer Contributed Retirement Plan – Depending on eligibility, employees receive an employer contributed retirement plan (no employee contribution required) and the option to contribute to a 403(b) using your own pre or post-tax dollars.
Full Suite of Health and Welfare plans including four medical plan options (including an HSA available option), dental, vision, life insurance, disability, EAP and more
Access to Flexible Spending Accounts (Medical/Dependent Care)
Competitive vacation and sick leave policies
Free, on-site parking

Receive, weigh, aliquot, extract, and prepare laboratory samples for analytical testing.
Perform routine sample processing, solution preparation, and sample cleanup following established laboratory protocols.
Support daily laboratory operations, including sample shipments, inventory management, consumable ordering, and equipment maintenance.
Operate laboratory equipment such as analytical balances, GenoGrinders, centrifuges, gas chromatographs, HPLC systems, and mass spectrometers.
Utilize Laboratory Information Management Systems (LIMS) to track samples, document activities, and maintain accurate laboratory records.
Assist with analytical testing and data generation in support of regulatory residue studies.

Maintain organized, accurate, and complete documentation.

Hands-on experience with quantitative weighing, sample extraction, and cleanup techniques involving complex agricultural or biological matrices.

Familiarity with HPLC, GC, and other analytical laboratory instrumentation.

new_jobs.title: Human Genetics and Genomic Curation Research Assistant (Research Data Assistant)
new_jobs.description:
MMGE - MOLECULAR GENETICS (IN-MOLG-IUINA)

One of the first human genetics departments in the country, the Department of Medical and Molecular Genetics at Indiana University (IU) School of Medicine has a rich history of training geneticists and genetic counselors and providing genetic consultation and counseling services. Currently ranked fifth in the nation among Genetics Departments for National Institutes of Health (NIH) Funding, received in 2023, the department contributes to the understanding of numerous genetic conditions through the integration of basic research in genetic and genomic mechanisms, translational research in disease models, and clinical trials in rare and common genetic diseases.

This research-focused position in the Azaiez-Booth Laboratory supports investigation of how genes and genetic variants contribute to human disease. The role combines scientific literature evaluation, genomic evidence curation, and research-data analysis across projects in human genetics and genomic medicine. Current activities include work with the ClinGen Hearing Loss Expert Panels, whose gene and variant classifications are publicly released and used by clinical laboratories to interpret genetic test results, as well as related laboratory and collaborative research projects.

Department-Specific Responsibilities

Evaluates and synthesizes scientific evidence, contributing to gene-disease and variant assessments, discusses findings with researchers, clinicians, and expert-panel members, and helps prepare presentations, reports, and manuscripts.
Identifies and critically reviews relevant scientific literature and genomic resources.
Extracts and synthesizes genetic, genomic, and clinical information, including population, segregation, functional, and computational evidence.
Applies established curation frameworks to prepare preliminary gene-disease validity assessments and variant evidence curations, documenting the rationale and questions requiring further scientific review.
Maintains accurate, well-documented research databases and curation records, including supporting references and assessment rationales.
Performs quality and consistency checks, synthesizes findings across curations and research datasets.
Conducts descriptive analyses to support laboratory and collaborative projects.
Prepares evidence summaries, tables, figures, and presentations.
Presents assigned work at laboratory and collaborative meetings, including virtual ClinGen Hearing Loss Expert Panel meetings; explains the evidence and criteria applied; and participates in scientific discussion.
Incorporates feedback and contributes to technical reports, grant progress reports, abstracts, and manuscript components.
Helps develop and improve research resources, templates, and procedural documentation.
Organizes assigned work, maintain clear records of progress and outstanding questions, and communicate with supervisors and collaborators to meet agreed priorities and timelines.

General Responsibilities

Assists with the research and collection of data from internal and/or external sources in support of research project(s).
Conducts descriptive analysis with collected data and assists with evaluative analysis.
Creates, updates, and maintains various databases and charts.
Prepares data analysis and grant reports for funding agencies.
Assists with creating technical reports, journal articles, and public presentations as needed.
May develop, schedule, or coordinate projects in support of research efforts.
May assist project personnel in the development of research projects.

Combinations of related education and experience may be considered. Education beyond the minimum required may be substituted for work experience. Work experience beyond the minimum required may be substituted for education.

EDUCATION

Required

Bachelor's degree (preferably in public policy, public administration, public health, social sciences, or a related field)

Preferred

Bachelor's degree in genetics, genomics, molecular biology, biology, biochemistry, biomedical sciences, neuroscience, bioinformatics, or a closely related scientific or health-related field
Coursework or additional training in human genetics, genomics, molecular genetics, genetic disease, molecular biology, bioinformatics, or a related biomedical discipline

Preferred

WORK EXPERIENCE

Some experience in a related field
Experience in an academic, clinical, laboratory, computational, or biomedical research setting; or work with human genetic, genomic, clinical, biological, or other scientific datasets
Prior gene or variant curation experience

Skills

Required

Proficient written and verbal communication skills
Maintains a high degree of professionalism
Demonstrated time management and priority setting skills
Demonstrates a high commitment to quality
Possesses flexibility to work in a fast paced, dynamic environment
Highly thorough and dependable
Familiarity with and openness to learn qualitative and mixed methods
Familiarity with statistical software preferred.
Must possess strong attention to detail.

This role requires the ability to effectively communicate and to operate a computer and other standard office productivity equipment. The position involves sedentary work as well as periods of time moving around an office environment and the campus. The person in this role must be able to perform the essential functions with or without an accommodation.

This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship.

Training in established research and curation methods will be provided, along with ongoing scientific mentorship.

The position offers the opportunity to build expertise in evaluating genetic evidence, a skill set relevant to careers in clinical genomics, genetic counseling, and biomedical research.

Prior Curation Experience Is Not Required.

new_jobs.description:
Job Summary
We are seeking a Software Engineer with a strong embedded systems background to design, develop, and execute validation test code for hardware and firmware platforms. In this role, you will analyze hardware schematics, datasheets, and firmware interface documentation to translate complex technical requirements into executable test scripts. Working in a fast-paced lab environment, you will handle on-demand test requests, validate behavior on embedded targets and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) setups, and drive root-cause failure analysis across hardware, firmware, and test-code layers.

Key Responsibilities
Requirement Translation & Test Development:
Read technical documentation—including schematics, datasheets, register maps, and firmware specs—to extract requirements and write original, executable test code in Python and Lua.
Rapid Prototyping & Execution:
Respond quickly to evolving and on-demand test requirements, delivering reliable validation code for embedded targets, bring-up boards, and HIL setups.
Code Quality & Debugging:
Write unit tests and actively debug your own code using debuggers, breakpoints, logging, and embedded debug tools (e.g., JTAG/SWD, serial consoles) rather than relying solely on end-to-end test reruns.
Failure Analysis & Triage:
Perform hands-on fault isolation, issue reproduction, and root-cause analysis by examining boot logs, panic/crash logs, core dumps, and device telemetry to separate hardware, firmware, and software issues.
Lab Validation:
Operate lab instrumentation—including oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, power supplies, and multimeters—to verify signal integrity, hardware interfaces, and device behavior.
Production & End-to-End Testing:
Execute dry runs, support hardware/firmware test stations, and run diagnostic tooling within production software environments.
Cross-Functional Collaboration:
Clearly document test findings and proactively communicate design decisions, workflows, and failure root causes to hardware, firmware, and software engineering teams.

Basic Qualifications (Must-Have)
Education:
BS or MS in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science (with an embedded focus), or equivalent practical experience.
Programming & Scripting:
Strong hands-on proficiency in Python (writing original code from scratch) and the ability to translate requirements into working scripts in real time (Python, Lua, etc.).
Embedded Systems:
Hands-on experience with firmware or embedded software on microcontrollers or SoCs, with a deep understanding of hardware-software interactions.
Hardware Protocols:
Working knowledge of communication interfaces and protocols including UART, SPI, I2C, USB, and CAN.
Hardware Validation & Lab Tools:
Proven experience with board bring-up, HIL testing, test fixtures, and using oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, multimeters, and power supplies.

new_jobs.title: Senior Staff Data Analyst
new_jobs.description:
Overview

Intuit is a global technology platform that helps consumers and small businesses overcome their most important financial challenges. Serving more than 100 million customers worldwide with TurboTax, Credit Karma, QuickBooks, and Mailchimp, we believe that everyone should have the opportunity to prosper. We never stop working to find new, innovative ways to make that possible.

The Strategic Research and Analytics team helps shape how we use data to inform strategies and investments across Marketing and Corporate Responsibility functions at Intuit. We are looking for a Senior Staff Data Analyst to set technical direction and own the measurement strategy for our most complex, ambiguous initiatives in data analytics, data science and data engineering. This role leads partnership across analysts, engineers, data scientists, researchers, marketers, communicators, and product managers, mentoring other analysts and setting the standard for how we deliver operational dashboards and analyses that drive business decisions. This person operates with a high degree of autonomy, translates ambiguous business questions into rigorous analytical frameworks, and regularly presents findings and recommendations to senior leadership. If you are an experienced analytics leader with strong technical depth and a passion for turning data into strategy, then this job is for you.

Responsibilities

Analytics Strategy & Business Impact

Own and drive the measurement strategy for high-priority initiatives across Intuit platform, establishing comprehensive KPI frameworks, leading indicators, and analytical approaches that connect activities and investments to business outcomes.
Define and advance a long-term analytics roadmap that anticipates evolving business needs, identifies strategic opportunities, and prioritizes capabilities that deliver measurable organizational value.
Serve as a strategic thought partner to senior leadership, translating complex business challenges into analytical strategies and evidence-based recommendations that inform priorities, investments, and decision-making.
Lead high-impact, cross-functional analytical initiatives that span multiple programs, stakeholders, and data domains, navigating ambiguity and aligning teams around shared objectives and measurable outcomes.
Proactively identify emerging trends, performance opportunities, and business risks, moving beyond descriptive reporting to deliver predictive and prescriptive insights that shape future strategies.

Advanced Analytics & Technical Leadership

Provide technical leadership in the design and application of advanced analytical methodologies, including experimentation, causal inference, incrementality measurement, attribution modeling, forecasting, and statistical modeling.
Establish rigorous analytical frameworks to evaluate the effectiveness of brand, reputation, internal and external communications, and corporate responsibility initiatives.
Lead the development of scalable measurement approaches that enable a holistic understanding of performance across channels, audiences, and initiatives.
Partner with data engineering, data science, and technology teams to influence data architecture, instrumentation, data pipelines, and analytical infrastructure that support reliable, scalable, and efficient decision-making.
Identify and champion opportunities to leverage emerging analytical techniques, automation, and AI-enabled capabilities to improve analytical efficiency, depth, and business impact.
Maintain hands-on technical expertise, independently conducting complex analyses, developing analytical prototypes, and solving challenging data problems when needed.

Qualifications

Qualifications

8+ years of experience working in a data analytics role supporting marketing and web, including leading complex, ambiguous analytical initiatives.
Bachelor’s Degree in Statistics, Math, Computer Science, Economics or related field; Master’s or PhD preferred.
Fluency in data analysis, including defining KPIs, statistical and predictive modeling concepts, descriptive statistics, customer segmentation, and funnel analysis.
Technical proficiency in SQL, Databricks, Qlik Sense, Tableau, and GitHub.
Hands-on expertise with Python and statistical modeling techniques (e.g. regression, classification, time series) to answer a wide range of measurement questions. Familiarity with market mix modeling and multi-touch attribution is a plus.
Hands-on experience with web analytics and clickstream data to support event tracking and instrumentation (e.g., Adobe Analytics, Segment, marketing attribution) preferred.
Meticulous attention to detail, with the ability to consistently produce accurate and error-free work even under tight deadlines.
Ability to tell stories clearly and concisely with data, and how they drive business outcomes.
Demonstrates strong business acumen and curiosity.
Ability to lead through influence across all levels and possess strong written and verbal communication skills. Outstanding communications skills with both technical and non-technical colleagues.
Excellent problem-solving skills and end-to-end quantitative thinking.
Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously to meet objectives and deadlines.
Proven experience mentoring or providing technical leadership to other analysts or data scientists.
Track record of setting analytics strategy and roadmaps for ambiguous, high-visibility initiatives, including presenting recommendations directly to senior leadership.

Intuit provides a competitive compensation package with a strong pay for performance rewards approach. This position may be eligible for a cash bonus, equity rewards and benefits, in accordance with our applicable plans and programs (see more about our compensation and benefits at Intuit®: Careers | Benefits). At Personalis, we are transforming the active management of cancer through breakthrough personalized testing. We aim to drive a new paradigm for cancer management, guiding care from biopsy through the life of the patient. Our highly sensitive assays combine tumor-and-normal profiling with proprietary algorithms to deliver advanced insights even as cancer evolves over time. Our products are designed to detect minimal residual disease (MRD) and recurrence at the earliest timepoints, enable selection of targeted therapies based on ultra-comprehensive genomic profiling, and enhance biomarker strategy for drug development. Personalis is based in Fremont, California.

Summary:

Serving as the Lab Manager for the R&D team, your primary responsibility will be overseeing R&D laboratory operations. You will manage laboratory supply inventories, own equipment maintenance and qualification, and partner with EHS to ensure compliance with safety standards. As schedule permits, you will also engage in hands-on activities to support collaborative R&D initiatives. Working alongside a world-class, dynamic team of scientists, assay developers, product managers, and clinicians, your work will contribute to a new generation of genomics-based precision medicine products in immuno-oncology and cancer clinical trials, diagnostics, and therapeutics used by pharma, biotech, hospitals, and clinicians.

Responsibilities

Laboratory Operations & Inventory Management: Oversee day-to-day operations across R&D laboratories. Track, maintain, and order reagents, consumables, and general laboratory supplies..
Equipment Maintenance & Compliance: Manage instrumentation maintenance, calibration, and troubleshooting. Lead definition, execution, and documentation of IQ/OQ/PQ protocols.
Safety: Partner with EHS to enforce safety standards, waste management, and space optimization.
Onboarding: Train and onboard new personnel on core laboratory instrumentation and procedures.
Collaborative Scientific Support (NGS Focus): As schedule permits, participate in hands-on R&D projects by performing DNA/RNA extraction, library preparation, and next-generation sequencing (NGS) assays.
Cross-Functional Communication: Actively participate in departmental scientific meetings, presenting updates on laboratory operations and experimental data to support team goals.

Qualifications

B.S. in a biological discipline with a minimum of 4 years of work experience or M.S. with 2 years of work experience in the life science industry.
Must have prior hands-on experience in lab management within a molecular biology laboratory environment.
Proven track record in laboratory inventory management, equipment maintenance, and space planning.
Strong organizational, communication, and problem-solving skills in a dynamic, high-energy environment.
Experience with next generation sequencing and liquid biopsy is a plus.

Employee Applicant Privacy Notice

Who we are:

Shape a brighter financial future with us.

Together with our members, we’re changing the way people think about and interact with personal finance.

We’re a next-generation financial services company and national bank using innovative, mobile-first technology to help our millions of members reach their goals. The industry is going through an unprecedented transformation, and we’re at the forefront. We’re proud to come to work every day knowing that what we do has a direct impact on people’s lives, with our core values guiding us every step of the way. Join us to invest in yourself, your career, and the financial world.

The Role:

The CTO Business Operations team enables SoFi’s Engineering, Product, and Design (EPD) organization to execute with operational rigor, financial discipline, and organizational clarity. We build and run the people-data pipelines, internal org tooling, and operating cadences that turn complex workforce and resource data into clear operational systems for the CTO and EPD leadership.

As a Data Analyst, you will own the data engineering, transforms, and reporting systems behind EPD headcount, organizational mapping, and org-wide resource reporting (:2,000+ people across Technology and Product). We are looking for a builder with strong data engineering foundations who wants to apply technical rigor to business operations: automating Workday people-data pipelines, evolving our resource reporting tools toward live API integration and self-serve leader workflows, running operating calendars, and supporting resource planning and software capitalization.

What you’ll do:

People Data Pipelines & Resource Reporting
Own and evolve our internal org and squad resource reporting (:2,000+ people across Engineering, Product, and Design), driving reliable biweekly refreshes and high data integrity.
Partner on the next evolution of our resource reporting tooling, moving from manual spreadsheet round-trips toward automated Workday API ingestion and interactive drag-and-drop seat management for engineering leaders.
Build and maintain automated people-data pipelines, Workday report transforms, and cross-system reconciliations across HRIS (Workday), Talent Acquisition, FP&A, and EPD rosters.
Maintain accurate org mapping across divisions, groups, and squads, tracking hiring progress, backfills, contingent workers, team movements, and capacity impacts.

Data Engineering, Automation & AI-Enabled Analytics
Take messy, multi-source operational datasets and build clean, repeatable data models, scripts, and validation checks that eliminate manual spreadsheet toil.
Use modern AI coding and analysis tools alongside SQL, Python (or equivalent scripting), and Google Sheets to rapidly prototype tooling, automate recurring reporting, and audit data quality.
Ensure strong data governance, schema consistency, and clear documentation across CTO Business Operations datasets and tools.

Operating Rhythms, Resource Planning & Capitalization
Manage and consolidate EPD operating calendars, leadership forum rhythms, and recurring readiness milestones across Technology and Product.
Support quarterly and annual headcount, contingent-worker, and resource planning cycles with clean baseline data, scenario models, and variance analysis.
Support the quarterly software development capitalization and labor allocation process in partnership with Finance, Accounting, and engineering leaders.
Perform ad-hoc analyses on organizational structure, squad composition, and workforce deployment to inform CTO leadership decisions.

Cross-Functional Partnership
Partner closely with CTO Business Operations, EPD leaders, People Partners, HRIS, Talent Acquisition, and Strategic Finance to keep staffing, org structure, and capacity data aligned.
Translate complex engineering and workforce inputs into structured metrics, clear narratives, and actionable recommendations.
Support executive-level summaries, dashboards, and operating materials for CTO leadership.

What You’ll Need:

4 to 7+ years of experience in data engineering, analytics engineering, technical business operations, or data analysis (targeting Staff level, or a strong Senior level with demonstrated technical depth).
Strong data engineering foundations: proven ability to ingest, clean, transform, and reconcile messy, multi-source datasets using SQL, Python (or Apps Script / TypeScript), and advanced Google Sheets / Excel.
Hands-on experience with Workday people data, custom reports, org hierarchies, and HRIS-to-planning reconciliations, with the ability to work toward API-driven data integrations.
Fluency with modern AI coding and data tools (e.g., Cursor, Claude, Copilot, LLM workflows) to accelerate pipeline development, data cleaning, and tooling, paired with strong judgment on output accuracy.
Track record of building and maintaining reliable internal tools, automated workflows, or operational dashboards for technical and executive stakeholders.
High attention to detail, operational rigor, and ownership mindset: you spot reconciliation gaps before leaders do and drive them to zero.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to operate independently in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment.
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering, Information Systems, Finance, Economics, or equivalent practical technical experience.
Bonus Points:
Prior background as a Data Engineer, Analytics Engineer, or HRIS / People Data Systems Engineer looking to build business and executive operations acumen.
Experience with Snowflake, Jira, and connecting project or engineering telemetry with workforce and resource data.
Experience building lightweight web interfaces, Apps Script automations, or interactive internal tools.
